bounded_statement: Within the supplied files, the report's selected result (two-sample Student t-test, t(10) = 3.0000, p = 0.0133, 95% CI 0.7719 to 5.2281, declared statistically significant at alpha = 0.05) is obtained by entering all 12 nubbin rows as independent observations, even though the data description designates colony_id as the independent unit and states that the two rows per colony are repeated measurements of the same coral. Re-running the same comparison on the 6 colony means (the authorized independent units, n = 3 per regime) preserves the mean difference of 3.000 mg CaCO3 g^-1 d^-1 but gives t(4) ≈ 2.078, p ≈ 0.106, 95% CI ≈ -1.01 to 7.01, so the report's significance conclusion is not supported at the declared unit of independence.

counterevidence_considered.description: The report is transparent about the clustered structure, correctly disclosing that only 6 colonies contributed 2 measurements each; this rules out a data-misreading explanation but does not repair the test's independence assumption.
counterevidence_considered.observed_value: 6 parent colonies, 2 measurements each, accurately reported

counterevidence_considered.description: The descriptive quantities are unaffected by the unit error: the mean difference of 3.000 mg CaCO3 g^-1 d^-1 is identical whether computed from nubbin rows or colony means (colonies are balanced with 2 nubbins each), so the effect direction and magnitude in the report are correct; only the inferential claim (p-value, CI, significance) is invalid.
counterevidence_considered.observed_value: mean difference 3.000 identical under row-level and colony-mean analysis

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I tried to falsify the issue in two ways. (1) I checked whether the row-level analysis could be defensible, i.e., whether nubbins might legitimately be independent units: the data description forecloses this by stating treatment was applied to whole colonies and that same-colony rows are repeated measurements of the same coral, and it names colony_id as the independent-unit column. (2) I checked materiality by recomputing the identical comparison at the authorized unit: colony means are ambient {13.0, 15.0, 17.0} and heated {10.5, 12.0, 13.5}; a pooled-variance two-sample t-test on these gives pooled variance 3.125, SE 1.4434, t(4) = 2.078, two-sided p ≈ 0.106, 95% CI ≈ (-1.01, 7.01). Since the report's significance claim (p = 0.0133 < 0.05) reverses to non-significance at the correct unit, the falsification fails and the issue stands as material. I also verified the report's own numbers (variances 3.6 and 2.4, pooled variance 3.0, SE 1.0, t = 3.0, p = 0.0133) reproduce from the 12 rows, confirming the reported result is exactly the row-level test rather than some other computation.

root_cause: The workflow pools rows purely by thermal_regime (rates_by_regime iterates over every CSV record and appends each nubbin's rate) and passes these row-level vectors directly to scipy.stats.ttest_ind, a procedure that assumes each entry is an independent observation. The colony_id column is read only to tally rows per colony for reporting, never to aggregate or model the within-colony dependence, so each of the 6 independent units (colonies) enters the row-independent t-test twice, inflating the effective sample size from 6 to 12 and the degrees of freedom from 4 to 10.
